name: Acid Green
lede: Acid green is a sharp, yellowish green whose history is thin, and the books read record the word more than the story.

sections.title: A bright green, not yet traced
sections.body:
Paterson defines acid green simply as a bright green, and he lists it among the green names [1]. The same dictionary uses the phrase for a dyestuff: acid colours include chromotrope, chrome brown, chromogen, acid green and alizarin yellow [1]. The books read do not connect the dye to the fashion color, so we do not claim the name comes from the dye [1].

The color word turns up in Jarman's book *Chroma*, in a scene where a woman wears acid green tights with a white lace miniskirt [2]. Our library's earliest source for the name is the xkcd survey of 2010, and the origin of the name is undocumented in our data [3].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch is a yellow-green, closest to the ISCC-NBS vivid yellow green, about five units away [3]. The xkcd survey gives a far brighter lime for the same name [3]. Related names are [[chartreuse]], [[lime-green]] and [[green]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: One painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color over at least five per cent of the canvas, George Bellows's 1916 [[painting:nga-61353|My Family]], where it covers about 8 per cent, as photographed [4].
